passage.text: When Emma first came to Bangkok as an exchange student, Nam took her to Chatuchak Weekend Market.
passage.reading: wɛn ˈɛmə ˈfɜːrst ˈkeɪm tə ˈbæŋkɑːk əz ən ɪksˈtʃeɪndʒ ˌstuːdənt, ˈnɑːm ˈtʊk hɜːr tə ˈtʃætuːtʃæk ˈwiːkɛnd ˈmɑːrkɪt.

passage.text: Emma loved it: there were thousands of shops selling clothes, plants, art and food.
passage.reading: ˈɛmə ˈlʌvd ɪt: ðɛr wɜːr ˈθaʊzəndz əv ˈʃɑːps ˈsɛlɪŋ ˈkloʊðz, ˈplænts, ˈɑːrt ənd ˈfuːd.

passage.text: At the first shop, she found a beautiful cotton bag.
passage.reading: ət ðə ˈfɜːrst ˈʃɑːp, ʃiː ˈfaʊnd ə ˈbjuːtəfəl ˈkɑːtən ˈbæɡ.
ˈhaʊ ˈmʌtʃ ɪz ɪt? ʃiː ˈæskt.
ˈeɪt ˈhʌndrəd ˈbɑːt, ˈsɛd ðə ˈʃɑːpkiːpər.

passage.text: Emma paid right away, and Nam laughed.
passage.reading: ˈɛmə ˈpeɪd ˈraɪt əˈweɪ, ənd ˈnɑːm ˈlæft.

passage.text: "Emma! That was only the starting price!"
passage.reading: ˈɛmə! ðæt wʌz ˈoʊnli ðə ˈstɑːrtɪŋ ˌpraɪs!

passage.text: "At markets like this, you can haggle. First, never accept the starting price.
passage.reading: ət ˈmɑːrkɪts ˈlaɪk ˈðɪs, juː kən ˈhæɡəl. ˈfɜːrst, ˈnɛvər əkˈsɛpt ðə ˈstɑːrtɪŋ ˌpraɪs.

passage.text: Offer about half, and smile. Haggling is a friendly game, not a fight.
passage.reading: ˈɔːfər əˈbaʊt ˈhæf, ənd ˈsmaɪl. ˈhæɡəlɪŋ ɪz ə ˈfrɛndli ˈɡeɪm, ˈnɑːt ə ˈfaɪt.

passage.text: If the price is still too high, just walk away. The shopkeeper often calls you back with a better price.
passage.reading: ɪf ðə ˈpraɪs ɪz ˈstɪl ˈtuː ˈhaɪ, ˈdʒʌst ˈwɔːk əˈweɪ. ðə ˈʃɑːpkiːpər ˈɔːfən ˈkɔːlz juː ˈbæk wɪð ə ˈbɛtər ˈpraɪs.

passage.text: But malls and supermarkets have fixed prices, so don't haggle there!"
passage.reading: bʌt ˈmɔːlz ənd ˈsuːpərmɑːrkɪts ˈhæv ˈfɪkst ˈpraɪsɪz, soʊ ˈdoʊnt ˈhæɡəl ˈðɛr!

passage.text: At the next shop, Emma saw a lamp that she liked.
passage.reading: ət ðə ˈnɛkst ˈʃɑːp, ˈɛmə ˈsɔː ə ˈlæmp ðæt ʃiː ˈlaɪkt.
ðə ˈstɑːrtɪŋ ˌpraɪs wʌz ˈsɪks ˈhʌndrəd ˈbɑːt.
ˈɛmə ˈsmaɪld ənd ˈsɛd, ˈhaʊ əˈbaʊt ˈθriː ˈhʌndrəd?

passage.text: In the end, she paid 400, and the shopkeeper smiled, too.
passage.reading: ɪn ði ˈɛnd, ʃiː ˈpeɪd ˈfɔːr ˈhʌndrəd, ənd ðə ˈʃɑːpkiːpər ˈsmaɪld, ˈtuː.

passage.text: "I love Thai markets," Emma said. "Shopping here is like a sport!"
passage.reading: aɪ ˈlʌv ˈtaɪ ˈmɑːrkɪts, ˈɛmə ˈsɛd. ˈʃɑːpɪŋ ˈhɪr ɪz ˈlaɪk ə ˈspɔːrt!
